defs_parts: Seven labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: Each editor dock has one job, and the Remote tab shows the running game.
A scene is a saved file, and the scene tree is what runs.
A signal tells you once, where polling asks on every tick.
The physics process function runs at a fixed rate on every machine.
A collision layer says where an object is, and a mask says what it scans.
The collision shape is what physics uses, not the sprite you see.
bookends.command: Quiz me on Godot terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms scene, scene tree, instance, signal, polling, input action, just-pressed, collision layer, collision mask and collision shape. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is a game-making situation, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike is wrong.
